Geographical senses II.2(a-d) mostly obsolete by late 16th century; assigned seat sense OE-1751; substitution expressions survive as literary/archaic; 1978 dialect 'stead of' is a distinct shortened construction. Attestations from OED supplied by author in this study, evidence IDs 129-138. Other meanings in OED: inhabited town II.3.a; farm/estate II.6; building site II.7; place in office III.11; aid/advantage IV.13.a. Manuscript compounds market-stead, woodstead, free-stead, wildstead are not presumed historically attested; compound investigations separate from this single-word row. No separate register row for compositional 'in the stead of' or other phrases; recorded as patterns in notes. No grammar entry recorded.

concepts: diminish; lessen; dwindle; decline; fade; weaken; pass away; draw to an end; ebb
notes: User chose Tier 1. Wōdlund manuscript usages include oracle's hold waned (power); waning of Elden Age and day/afternoon/hour/moments waned (time passing toward end); waning light and hall waned dim (light); voice waned strange and grave, yet grim (lingering voice and its fading impression). Author explains 'moments waned strange/grim' as time passing while the moment has a strange or dire character, not becoming strange because of waning; voice is lingering/fading after speech; 'The hour wanes long—beyond its time' means the allotted hour is spent yet work remains, holding tension of passing time and prolonged duty. These full expressive constructions are authorial extensions; OED I.3 attests nonce adjective complements 'waned faint' (1837), 'waned grey' (1850); OED I.6 time period 1590 onward; MED 1.c temporal diminution c1175 (?OE). Do not claim exact whole strings attested. EarlyPrint author's [word="wane"] KWIC export 1383 hits across 1089 documents, also many noun, proper-name or unrelated hits; grouped-year list is aggregate metadata, not independently dated quotations. User-supplied OED and MED records in evidence 139-151. No extra grammar row or separate idiom registered.

concepts: grow; increase; become; turn; intensify; strengthen; brighten; develop; deepen; swell; wax and wane
notes: User selected Tier 1. Old English weaxan, Germanic strong verb with past weox and participle weaxen; later waxed. This register is ONLY the grow/become verb OED wax v1 / MED waxen v.(1); NOT coat-with-wax MED waxen v.(2). Wōdlund manuscript uses include eyes waxing dark; waxed wary; thoughts waxed inward; waxing silence; boldness waxing with every word; strange it waxed and stranger yet; vision waxed dim; wax whole; voice waxed soft; waxing brighter; white light waxed; waxing stronger and keener; smile waxed full; waxed full wild; cheer waxed heavy. Historically attested whole construction wax + adjective can mean turn or become and may denote diminished magnitude: MED sun 'vex al wan', OED waxed scant, waxed fainter, waxeth smaller. No claim every authorial expression is exactly attested. EarlyPrint user search [word="wax"] supplied 25516 matches, 8010 documents and year grouping; includes wax noun and separate coating verb, so not a pure grow-verb frequency. OED/MED provide dated evidence rows 152-175; EarlyPrint KWIC includes wax warie, wild, eyes dimme and voice domb but metadata dates not verified.
